messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: high-severity - serving-runtime NCCL communicator failures in us-west-2 (model: rw/fast-13b) - multiple pods reporting 'ncclCommInitRank failed' and CUDA OOMs. Impact: degraded throughput and 502s for ~12% of requests. Auto-escalation to oncall.
alex: Got paged. I'm looking. Which pool is this hitting? gw-ptp-prod-usw2?
jamie: Yep, gw-ptp-prod-usw2. Noticed increased collector errors, then pods started restarting. Root container logs show NCCL errors then CUDA driver resets.
sanjay: Pasting recent pod log snippet:
```
I0112 03:21:10.123456 1 nccl_wrapper.cc:214] ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled system error
E0112 03:21:10.123457 1 cuda_runtime.cc:88] CUDA error: out of memory (driver shutting down)
I0112 03:21:10.123458 1 kubelet: container_restart backoff
```
maria: Also seeing kernel log on host gpunode-13:
```
[  112.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=19283, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  112.346000] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.1: mlx5_core: async event: port state change event: DOWN
```
alex: So both GPU and IB events. Likely either NV driver + mlx mismatch or IB flaps making NCCL hang and then driver resets. First step: stop scheduling new TP jobs on that pool and failover to single-GPU shards.
jamie: I'm going to put a temporary placement constraint on the model route to avoid multi-GPU placements in us-west-2: `route:update rw/fast-13b --placement avoid:gw-ptp-prod-usw2`.
sanjay: Also recommend setting NCCL environment fallbacks for affected pods while we investigate: `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` or `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` as a quick test to skip IB. That will increase latency but avoid hangs.
alex: Doing a graceful node drain on gpunode-13 to see if issues stop. Marking node unschedulable.
ops-bot: Node gpunode-13 cordon succeeded.
alex: Evicting pods from that node now.
maria: Heads-up: a few customers on dedicated pool may see degraded throughput while we move traffic. Sam from CS, expect some inbound tickets.
sam-cs: Noted. I'll post a short status update to the affected customer list and ask for patience. ETA for next update 30m.
jamie: I triggered a rolling restart of the runtime pods in the pool with the fallback env var set. Command used:
```
kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 -n prod-usw2
kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime -n prod-usw2
```
alex: After rollout, early telemetry shows 50% drop in NCCL errors but a few pods still hitting CUDA resets. Those are the ones on gpunode-13 which I drained.
sanjay: I ran nccl tests on the node after cordon. Observed packet drops on mlx5 link:
```
ethtool -S mlx5_core | grep rx_err
rx_err: 142
```
maria: Opening ticket with infra to check switch port and driver versions. Suspect firmware mismatch after recent patching window.
ops-bot: infra-ticket #INC-2026 opened: "mlx5 link flaps -> NCCL timeouts". Assigned to infra-net.
jamie: For customers currently impacted, we routed to single-GPU shards and enabled software fallback; error rate dropped to ~1.8% now. SLO alert still firing, but recovering.
alex: Can we also add conservative NCCL_TIMEOUT env override to give time for slow reconnects? e.g., `NCCL_TIMEOUT=300`.
sanjay: We should be cautious—raising timeout can make hangs persist longer; better to reduce TP size and avoid collective across flaky links. For long-term, recommend NIC firmware rollback or upgrade consistent with GPU driver.
alex: Agree. Short-term action list:
- keep node cordoned until infra confirms link stable (alex)
- route fast-13b away from multi-GPU placements in us-west-2 (jamie)
- set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for runtime as hotfix (jamie)
- notify CS and customers (sam)
- infra to triage switch and driver mismatch (maria/ops)
I'll take incident lead. Paging rotation: handing to night oncall at 1812345900 (jamie please ack handoff).
jamie: Ack. I'll cover night monitoring and escalate to infra if errors reappear. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment rollout completed for serving-runtime 0.21.4 -> with env NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
maria: Infra found that one of the spine switches had a bad transceiver causing intermittent link errors on ports servicing gpunode-12..15. Replaced transceiver and tested link — errors dropped to zero.
sanjay: After transceiver replacement I re-ran NCCL smoke tests across 4 GPUs on a clean node and saw stable collects. No more 'ncclCommInitRank failed'.
alex: Uncordoning gpunode-13 after infra confirms link stable and kernel driver OK.
ops-bot: Node gpunode-13 uncordon succeeded.
jamie: Rolling back NCCL_IB_DISABLE now that IB is healthy to restore performance for TP workloads.
```
kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime NCCL_IB_DISABLE-
kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime -n prod-usw2
```
alex: Monitoring matrix: CPU/GPU utilization, NCCL error rates, pod restarts. Will keep this thread updated. Preliminary impact summary for postmortem:
- Root cause: intermittent mlx5 transceiver failure caused IB packet loss -> NCCL timeouts -> GPU driver resets
- Blast radius: multi-GPU placements in us-west-2 for rw/fast-13b and related TP jobs (~12% of requests experienced 502s)
- Mitigations: cordon/evict affected nodes, transceiver replacement, temporary env fallback (NCCL_IB_DISABLE), routing away from multi-GPU placements
- Customer impact: transient degraded throughput and increased error rate for ~45 minutes, CS notified
- Next steps: schedule firmware/firmware+driver compatibility sweep, add proactive link error alerting, add automatic routing fallback when NCCL errors spike
sam-cs: I'll prepare a short customer postmortem and share with the CS list when you have the final impact window.
maria: I'll file infra RCA and include ticket logs + switch telemetry.
alex: Thanks everyone. Jamie, handing the incident to you for night watch. Please reopen if any recurrence. :white_check_mark:
